chunks.arabic_text: ٣٤ - مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُطَّلِبِ، الشَّيْبَانِيُّ، أَبُو الْمُفَضَّلِ.

translations.en: 34 – Muḥammad b. ʿAbdullāh b. Muḥammad b. al-Muṭṭalib, al-Shaybānī, Abū Mufaḍḍal.

chunks.arabic_text: وَضَّاعٌ، كَثِيرُ الْمَنَاكِرِ. رَأَيْتُ كُتُبَهُ، وَفِيهَا الْأَسَانِيدُ مِنْ دُونِ الْمَتُونِ، وَالْمُتُونُ مِنْ دُونِ الْأَسَانِيدِ. وَأَرَى تَرْكَ مَا يَنْفُرُّ بِهِ.

translations.en: A fabricator, (he narrated) much that is denied. I saw his books and in them are isnads without texts and texts without isnads. And I regard (that one must) abandon what he exclusively (narrates).

en.summary: Al-Ghadā'iri critiques Muḥammad b. ʿAbdullāh al-Shaybānī for his 'kathīr al-manākīr' (frequent fabrication), specifically highlighting the structural defect where his manuscripts separate chains of narrators (isnād) from the text (matn), indicating a lack of rigorous compilation. This specific criticism reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying the integrity of transmission structures to distinguish authentic teachings from those of lesser narrators, leading to the recommendation of withholding his unique narrations (istikhbār) from legal derivation.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Shayani and why is he considered a fabricator?
